df-001: Server fetches profile image from requester-supplied URL (HTTP)
df-002: POST of challenge solution notification to configured webhook (HTTP)
df-003: Chatbot requests to configured OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint (HTTP) df-003 authentication: LLM_API_KEY configured on the provider client; evidence: routes/chat.ts:110
df-004: Startup GET /models to check configured LLM model availability (HTTP)
df-005: NFTMinted contract event subscription over WebSocket RPC (WSS) df-006: ContractExploited contract event subscription over WebSocket RPC (WSS)

df-008: Login query looking up user by email and password hash (SQL) df-008 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-009: Sequelize ORM access to SQLite database (SQLite) df-009 authentication: Embedded SQLite engine inside the application process; the engine has no login of its own.; evidence: models/index.ts:34

df-011: OAuth authorization (HTTPS) df-011 authentication: The identity provider authenticates the user at its sign-in endpoint; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148
df-012: OAuth profile request (HTTPS) df-012 authentication: The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68

df-013: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-013 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:52, routes/dataExport.ts:18, routes/orderHistory.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:156
df-014: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP) df-015: API requests (unknown authentication) (HTTP)
df-017: API requests (bearer) (HTTP) df-017 authentication: the handler checks a bearer credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: lib/insecurity.ts:52

df-019: Direct requests (cookie) (HTTP) df-019 authentication: the handler checks a cookie credential and rejects the request without it; evidence: routes/profileImageFileUpload.ts:35, routes/profileImageUrlUpload.ts:21, routes/userProfile.ts:34, routes/updateUserProfile.ts:17, routes/dataErasure.ts:26, routes/dataErasure.ts:76
Internet Attacker → C-03 · Juice Shop Express API: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
Internet Attacker → C-09 · Authentication & Session Surface: scenario 2, 3, 5; its findings also affect C-01 · Sequelize application data access
Internet Attacker → C-04 · Web3 / Wallet / NFT Surface: scenario 3, 5
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6
Dynamic code evaluation — evidence: lib/xml.ts:12, lib/xml.ts:38, routes/b2bOrder.ts:23, routes/captcha.ts:22

Further capabilities: WebSocket endpoint — evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:20, lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23; Blockchain client — evidence: routes/nftMint.ts:18, routes/web3Wallet.ts:20
C-03 · Juice Shop Express API: LLM provider API key

C-07 · SQLite Embedded Database: User credentials and accounts

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
trust change within a column (dashed: inferred)
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE category: filled = findings in that category
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Crafted input runs code on the server
The recipient performs no authentication check on this connection.
The recipient checks the token supplied with the request.
A session cookie identifies the caller.
The caller presents a configured service credential.
Delegated access; only the evidenced protocol step is covered.
Authentication could not be determined from the code.
Numbered hexagon: authentication · circle: attack scenario
Red: absent / unsafe · yellow: standard / limited · green: stronger
Method properties, not proof of a secure implementation.
Components are ordered within their layer to reduce line crossings, not by
